items.problem: Migrating UWP in-process background tasks: the agent hit CS0246/CS0115 on App.OnBackgroundActivated and then two Appx registration failures (0x80080204 / 0x80073CF6) from the windows.backgroundTasks manifest extension, taking ~5 build/launch cycles.
items.evidence: build-events turn 36 'App.xaml.cs(21,29): error CS0115: App.OnBackgroundActivated(...) no suitable method found to override'; turn 30 'CS0246 BackgroundActivatedEventArgs could not be found'; validator turn 48 WARN 'manifest is invalid … not allowed to have EntryPoint="Tasks.ActivitySensorBackgroundTask" without ActivatableClassId'; Test-AppLaunch turn 51 'extension is missing an EntryPoint or StartPage attribute (0x80073CF6)'. Resolved turns 37/52 by deleting the override + manifest extension and wrapping Register() in try/catch.
items.covered_at: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md '## Background Tasks' (anchor #background-tasks, line ~321) and '## Application Lifecycle and Activation' (line ~302).
items.proposed_improvement: Extend the existing Background Tasks section with the two concrete WinUI 3 failure modes and their fixes: (1) DELETE any App.OnBackgroundActivated override — Microsoft.UI.Xaml.Application has no such method (CS0115/CS0246); (2) REMOVE the <Extension Category="windows.backgroundTasks"> element from Package.appxmanifest — an in-process EntryPoint there makes the package fail to register/launch (0x80080204 / 0x80073CF6); (3) wrap BackgroundTaskBuilder.Register() in try/catch per the skill's existing 'Defensive UI for device-dependent features' rule.
items.generalizes: Every UWP sample using IBackgroundTask + a windows.backgroundTasks manifest extension + an OnBackgroundActivated dispatcher hits the same three failures on WinUI 3. The section already exists, so sharpening it (not adding a new topic) directly unblocks the recurring background-task migration.
